why: Copy a person reads that is still written in the code rather than in _locales. The map is empty as of 2026-08-20: B-75 is paid in full, every sentence this tool can see is in _locales, and the exact-match rule still stands — a new entry here is a regression that has to be argued for, not a number to top up. The file is kept rather than deleted, and that is the deliberate part. Its own measurer is known to be partly blind (B-76): two classes of sentence defeat the anchor, and four live strings were found by reading after this tool had called their files clean. Deleting the ledger the moment the number reached zero would turn 'the tool found nothing' into 'there is nothing', which is the one substitution this project refuses everywhere else. It goes when B-76 lands and the closing line can make the stronger claim honestly.
rule: Exact match. A file with more hits than its entry is a regression; a file with fewer means the debt was paid and the number here has to come down in the same change. Both are refusals, because a ceiling nobody lowers is a ceiling that rots upward.
paidSoFar: core-recovery closed 2026-08-20: 18 step sentences and 6 portable lines moved to _locales. The package keeps the id, the order and `elsewhere` — the facts it actually decides — and `packages/ui/src/recovery/recovery.ts` maps id to key through two `*_KEY` tables, which is the shape the locale gate reads: a computed key would make all eighteen messages look dead to it. The assertions about the words moved to the surface's test rather than being deleted with the words. core-download closed the same day: five headlines and five shape sentences became codes, and the codes now cross the `download/verdict` RPC — the background used to compose English and send it. `reasons` deliberately stayed words, because those come from the checks and whoever ran them had already resolved them through the catalogue. core-credential closed the same day: seven credential facts and five password explanations became codes, and one of them had been formatting a number with `toLocaleString('en')` — an English thousands separator chosen inside a package with no business knowing the reader's locale, and invisible to this sweep because it is not a quoted string. The count travels as a number now. core-gate and core-extensions closed 2026-08-20. The gate's `explain` was a finished sentence beside a `reason` that already said the same thing as a code, so the sentence is gone rather than moved: `describes` carries the action, `detail` the browser's own words about a surface that would not open, and `apps/extension/src/background/gate-words.ts` words the seven reasons. core-extensions gave up five change sentences, two analysis caveats and a hex density that arrived as English prose with the number already inside it — `InventoryChange` is a discriminated union now, so a `host-access-widened` without its hosts fails to compile instead of rendering a sentence with a hole in it, and the wording lives behind a second export path, `@okolos/ui/words`, because two surfaces need the same sentence and pulling the whole UI graph into the worker for a lookup table is not a trade worth making. Both write `explainKey` + `explainArgs` into the journal rather than a resolved sentence: `summarise` in the popup resolves at read time, so a reader who switches language sees their own words on old rows — and the extensions journal's dedup, which used to compare the sentence, compares those values, or a change of language alone would rewrite every unaccepted row and push `createdAt` to today. Two blind spots in the sweep were found by reading rather than by the tool, and both are recorded as B-76: a sentence whose first word ends in a colon (`'Blocked: this page…'`) breaks the three-word anchor, and a nested quote inside a template substitution (`` `${n} thing${n === 1 ? '' : 's'} worth a look.` ``) truncates the literal before the sentence starts. The second one was live in `packages/ui/src/extensions/extensions.ts` and is fixed here; the ceiling never counted either of them, which is the point of the row. Paid in full 2026-08-20. The last instalment closed `storage/export.ts`, `core-feeds`, `core-injection/stage1.ts`, `background/feeds.ts` and `background/leaks.ts`. `exportAll` now takes an `ExportWords` — the note inside the downloaded file and the marker beside each omission are the reader's words, while the decision about what is withheld stays with the data; `WITHHELD_MARKER` shrank to the searchable token `[withheld]` so that "is anything withheld from this file" is answerable in any locale. `core-feeds` gave up six refusal sentences for a `Refusal` union, and its one genuinely two-message case (`bad-signature` with and without something to fall back on) is decided on the surface, because with nothing kept there is no version to substitute. Two of the eleven were not translations at all: `('high' as const)` is a false positive of the anchor, exempt with that reason, and `OUR_FEEDS.en` is the name `apps/proxy` prints on public pages from a worker with no `_locales`. Its docstring said "for the worker", and the extension's own service worker read that as itself — two sentences were pulling an English list name into Russian prose, fixed in the same change. The closing line of the sweep now says "nothing the sweep can see", which is what it can support.
